cards.front: Complete the rule: The handbook’s pedestrian category includes people walking, skating.
cards.back: The handbook’s pedestrian category includes people walking, skating in-line or riding skateboards, including people with physical, hearing or visual disabilities.
cards.memory_hook: Pedestrian category includes varied travelers

cards.front: Complete the rule: Drivers should be ready to yield and.
cards.back: Drivers should be ready to yield and avoid passing unnecessarily close to people on foot.
cards.memory_hook: Prepare to yield and leave pedestrian

cards.front: Complete the rule: A pedestrian crossing outside a marked or unmarked.
cards.back: A pedestrian crossing outside a marked or unmarked crosswalk must yield to drivers and should use an available pedestrian bridge or tunnel.
cards.memory_hook: Outside crosswalk pedestrian yields

cards.front: Complete the rule: A pedestrian should use a sidewalk or shoulder.
cards.back: A pedestrian should use a sidewalk or shoulder when available; when walking on a two-way roadway is necessary, face approaching traffic and stay away from the traveled edge.
cards.memory_hook: Walk facing traffic when roadway use

cards.front: Complete the rule: Do not walk on a highway.
cards.back: Do not walk on a highway while impaired by alcohol or other drugs.
cards.memory_hook: Impaired walking is unsafe

cards.front: Complete the rule: A pedestrian using a guide dog, white cane.
cards.back: A pedestrian using a guide dog, white cane, wheelchair or another assistive device has the same pedestrian rights and must receive the right of way.
cards.memory_hook: Assistive device preserves pedestrian priority

cards.front: Complete the rule: Walkers and joggers should use provided paths, choose.
cards.back: Walkers and joggers should use provided paths, choose wide shoulders when using roads, face traffic and look and listen for vehicles.
cards.memory_hook: Paths and observation support safe walking

cards.front: Complete the rule: At night or in poor visibility, walkers and.
cards.back: At night or in poor visibility, walkers and joggers should choose well-lit areas and wear reflective clothing.
cards.memory_hook: Low visibility calls for lighting and

cards.front: Complete the rule: Pedestrians must comply with railway.
cards.back: Pedestrians must comply with railway gates, bridge gates and other barriers.
cards.memory_hook: Pedestrians obey crossing barriers

cards.front: Complete the rule: Standing in the roadway to hitchhike is illegal.
cards.back: Standing in the roadway to hitchhike is illegal, and pedestrians should not solicit money or business on or beside a highway.
cards.memory_hook: Do not solicit rides from roadway

cards.front: Complete the rule: A person at least eighteen may skate on.
cards.back: A person at least eighteen may skate on a public roadway from sunrise to sunset when its posted limit is forty-five miles per hour or lower and traffic is not obstructed.
cards.memory_hook: Road skating has age time and

cards.front: Complete the rule: Watch for child-hazard locations such as schools, parks.
cards.back: Watch for child-hazard locations such as schools, parks, playgrounds and bus stops, and prepare to slow where children are likely.
cards.memory_hook: Expect children near their activity areas

cards.front: Complete the rule: Use exceptional care while backing in a driveway.
cards.back: Use exceptional care while backing in a driveway near children, and keep children’s play away from streets, driveways and other hazardous areas.
cards.memory_hook: Backing and play areas need special

cards.front: Complete the rule: Parents should teach pedestrian rights and.
cards.back: Parents should teach pedestrian rights and responsibilities to children while they are young.
cards.memory_hook: Teach pedestrian responsibilities early

cards.front: Complete the rule: Motorcyclists share other road users’ rights and responsibilities.
cards.back: Motorcyclists share other road users’ rights and responsibilities, but their small size can make them difficult to detect and can lead drivers to underestimate their speed.
cards.memory_hook: Small motorcycle may be overlooked

cards.front: Complete the rule: Expect motorcycles in traffic throughout the year.
cards.back: Expect motorcycles in traffic throughout the year and check carefully before turning across their path.
cards.memory_hook: Expect motorcycles in every season

cards.front: Complete the rule: When turning left across opposing traffic, yield to.
cards.back: When turning left across opposing traffic, yield to motorcycles and wait until the rider’s intent is clear.
cards.memory_hook: Left turn driver yields to motorcycle

cards.front: Complete the rule: A motorcycle rider may proceed after a red.
cards.back: A motorcycle rider may proceed after a red signal fails to change for one hundred twenty seconds, but must first yield to approaching traffic.
cards.memory_hook: Motorcycle signal exception still yields

cards.front: Complete the rule: A motorcyclist is entitled to the entire lane.
cards.back: A motorcyclist is entitled to the entire lane and needs room to maneuver, so a car driver must not share that lane beside the motorcycle.
cards.memory_hook: Motorcycle receives full lane

cards.front: Complete the rule: When a motorcycle passes, hold your speed and.
cards.back: When a motorcycle passes, hold your speed and lane position and allow the rider to complete the pass and return to a proper position.
cards.memory_hook: Steady position helps motorcycle finish passing

cards.front: Complete the rule: Follow a motorcycle with a gap of at.
cards.back: Follow a motorcycle with a gap of at least three to four seconds, and dim headlights when following it as with other vehicles.
cards.memory_hook: Motorcycle needs following space and dimmed

cards.front: Complete the rule: On dry pavement a motorcycle can stop sooner.
cards.back: On dry pavement a motorcycle can stop sooner than a car, although the rider’s training and experience affect stopping ability.
cards.memory_hook: Motorcycle stopping ability can differ

cards.front: Complete the rule: Wet or icy surfaces reduce a motorcycle’s braking.
cards.back: Wet or icy surfaces reduce a motorcycle’s braking and maneuvering ability, while wind gusts can move it significantly across its lane.
cards.memory_hook: Weather changes motorcycle control

cards.front: Complete the rule: Debris, potholes, oil, gravel and railway tracks can.
cards.back: Debris, potholes, oil, gravel and railway tracks can cause a motorcycle to change position or slow where a car might continue normally.
cards.memory_hook: Road hazards may change rider position

cards.front: Complete the rule: Use extreme caution and seek emergency.
cards.back: Use extreme caution and seek emergency medical help after a motorcycle crash.
cards.memory_hook: Motorcycle crash calls for emergency assistance

cards.front: Complete the rule: An autocycle has three wheels, a steering wheel.
cards.back: An autocycle has three wheels, a steering wheel and non-straddling seating; roadway use requires proper title and registration and a valid Illinois driver’s license.
cards.memory_hook: Autocycle differs from straddled motorcycle

cards.front: Complete the rule: On most roads, bicyclists have roadway rights and.
cards.back: On most roads, bicyclists have roadway rights and responsibilities, including the right of way; the handbook includes qualifying electric and gas-assisted bicycles in this comparison.
cards.memory_hook: Bicycles are road users with rights

cards.front: Complete the rule: A designated bicycle lane cannot be used by.
cards.back: A designated bicycle lane cannot be used by a motor vehicle for travel, parking, idling or passenger pickup or drop-off even when no cyclist is present.
cards.memory_hook: Empty bicycle lane is still reserved

cards.front: Complete the rule: A cyclist may need to leave a bicycle.
cards.back: A cyclist may need to leave a bicycle lane, and drivers should be ready to move around the rider safely.
cards.memory_hook: Expect cyclist outside marked bike lane

cards.front: Complete the rule: Bicycles travel with vehicle traffic, and hazards or.
cards.back: Bicycles travel with vehicle traffic, and hazards or a narrow lane may require a rider to move toward the lane’s center.
cards.memory_hook: Cyclist follows traffic but may need

cards.front: Complete the rule: Two cyclists may ride abreast if normal traffic.
cards.back: Two cyclists may ride abreast if normal traffic is not impeded; more than two abreast is prohibited outside areas reserved for bicycles.
cards.memory_hook: Two abreast riding has traffic condition

cards.front: Complete the rule: Yield to a cyclist as to another.
cards.back: Yield to a cyclist as to another vehicle and never crowd or threaten the rider.
cards.memory_hook: Cyclist receives vehicle like priority

decks.module: Bicycle passing and Electric bicycle locations

cards.front: Complete the rule: Pass a cyclist slowly with at least three.
cards.back: Pass a cyclist slowly with at least three feet measured from the vehicle’s side-mirror edge; if that space is unavailable, wait until passing can be done safely.
cards.memory_hook: Measure bicycle clearance from mirror

cards.front: Complete the rule: Passing too close to a cyclist and causing.
cards.back: Passing too close to a cyclist and causing a crash may expose the driver to criminal charges.
cards.memory_hook: Close pass causing crash can be

cards.front: Complete the rule: When following bicycles, leave generous room, be ready.
cards.back: When following bicycles, leave generous room, be ready to stop quickly and take extra care in bad weather.
cards.memory_hook: Following cyclist requires room and readiness

cards.front: Complete the rule: Do not use high beams when.
cards.back: Do not use high beams when meeting an oncoming cyclist at night.
cards.memory_hook: Dim lights for approaching cyclist

cards.front: Complete the rule: Before turning left, allow an opposing cyclist through.
cards.back: Before turning left, allow an opposing cyclist through; if sharing a left-turn lane with a cyclist, remain behind until the rider completes the turn.
cards.memory_hook: Left turn motorist waits for cyclist

cards.front: Complete the rule: Before turning right, allow a cyclist approaching on.
cards.back: Before turning right, allow a cyclist approaching on the right to continue through the intersection and signal the intended turn.
cards.memory_hook: Do not turn right across approaching

cards.front: Complete the rule: Check for cyclists before opening a parked vehicle’s.
cards.back: Check for cyclists before opening a parked vehicle’s door, and consider reaching with the right hand to help look behind.
cards.memory_hook: Look for bikes before opening door

cards.front: Complete the rule: A low-speed electric bicycle has usable pedals and.
cards.back: A low-speed electric bicycle has usable pedals and an electric motor rated below seven hundred fifty watts.
cards.memory_hook: Electric bicycle requires pedals and limited

cards.front: Complete the rule: Low-speed electric bicycles may use authorized roads, bicycle.
cards.back: Low-speed electric bicycles may use authorized roads, bicycle lanes and paths but not sidewalks, and local authorities may prohibit them on local roads or paths.
cards.memory_hook: Electric bicycle access depends on authorization

decks.module: Electric bicycle classes and Electric scooters

cards.front: Complete the rule: A Class One electric bicycle assists only while.
cards.back: A Class One electric bicycle assists only while the rider pedals and ends assistance at twenty miles per hour.
cards.memory_hook: Class One pedal assistance with cutoff

cards.front: Complete the rule: A Class Two electric bicycle can propel itself.
cards.back: A Class Two electric bicycle can propel itself using its motor, but its motor cannot engage when the bicycle reaches twenty miles per hour.
cards.memory_hook: Class Two allows motor only propulsion

cards.front: Complete the rule: The handbook’s Class Three electric-bicycle description requires pedaling.
cards.back: The handbook’s Class Three electric-bicycle description requires pedaling for motor engagement and a rider aged at least sixteen.
cards.memory_hook: Class Three needs pedaling and minimum

cards.front: Complete the rule: A scooter can be titled and registered in.
cards.back: A scooter can be titled and registered in Illinois if it has a federal safety-certification label and a vehicle identification number.
cards.memory_hook: Road scooter needs identification and certification

cards.front: Complete the rule: Scooter and moped drivers must follow signs, signals.
cards.back: Scooter and moped drivers must follow signs, signals and traffic laws, and carrying a passenger requires a passenger seat and footrest.
cards.memory_hook: Passenger scooter needs passenger equipment

cards.front: Complete the rule: An engine below one hundred fifty cubic centimeters.
cards.back: An engine below one hundred fifty cubic centimeters places a scooter in the motor-driven-cycle category requiring a Class L motorcycle license; at least that displacement requires Class M.
cards.memory_hook: Scooter displacement determines motorcycle class

cards.front: Complete the rule: A moped may be driven with any valid.
cards.back: A moped may be driven with any valid Illinois driver’s license; a combustion-powered moped cannot exceed fifty cubic centimeters or require manual gear shifting.
cards.memory_hook: Moped qualification has engine and shifting

cards.front: Complete the rule: A low-speed electric scooter weighs less than one.
cards.back: A low-speed electric scooter weighs less than one hundred pounds, has two or three wheels, handlebars and a standing floorboard, and reaches no more than ten miles per hour using electric and human propulsion.
cards.memory_hook: Low speed scooter has specific design

cards.front: Complete the rule: A low-speed electric-scooter operator must be at least.
cards.back: A low-speed electric-scooter operator must be at least eighteen, needs no license and may use a road, trail or sidewalk only where the municipality or park district permits it.
cards.memory_hook: Adult scooter use requires local permission

cards.front: Complete the rule: Only one person may ride a low-speed electric.
cards.back: Only one person may ride a low-speed electric scooter, which needs a headlamp and a red rear reflector or lamp.
cards.memory_hook: Single rider and required lights

cards.front: Complete the rule: Stay clear of a large vehicle’s blind spots.
cards.back: Stay clear of a large vehicle’s blind spots and keep a position its driver can see in the side mirrors.
cards.memory_hook: Stay visible to large vehicle driver

cards.front: Complete the rule: Watch large-vehicle signals and allow wide turns, including.
cards.back: Watch large-vehicle signals and allow wide turns, including a possible open space on the right just before a truck turns right.
cards.memory_hook: Do not crowd wide truck turn

cards.front: Complete the rule: Give large vehicles additional space because their.
cards.back: Give large vehicles additional space because their weight and size affect stopping and maneuvering.
cards.memory_hook: Large size needs extra space

cards.front: Complete the rule: Dim headlights when following a truck at night.
cards.back: Dim headlights when following a truck at night because bright reflections in its large mirrors can blind its driver.
cards.memory_hook: Dim following lights behind truck

cards.front: Complete the rule: The handbook suggests a headlight blink to notify.
cards.back: The handbook suggests a headlight blink to notify a truck driver of a pass, especially at night, and advises finishing promptly rather than remaining beside the truck.
cards.memory_hook: Notify truck and avoid lingering alongside

cards.front: Complete the rule: On a four-lane highway, move away from a.
cards.back: On a four-lane highway, move away from a disabled vehicle showing hazard lights when a safe lane change is possible; otherwise slow down and keep the reduced speed until well beyond it.
cards.memory_hook: Move over or slow for disabled

cards.front: Complete the rule: Do not push a disabled vehicle along a.
cards.back: Do not push a disabled vehicle along a rural highway except in an emergency, and remove it so it does not remain a hazard.
cards.memory_hook: Rural pushing has emergency limitation

cards.front: Complete the rule: Removing a damaged vehicle from the road also.
cards.back: Removing a damaged vehicle from the road also requires removal of its glass and other debris.
cards.memory_hook: Clear crash debris with vehicle

cards.front: Complete the rule: Towing one vehicle with another requires a drawbar.
cards.back: Towing one vehicle with another requires a drawbar, usually no more than fifteen feet between vehicles, and two connecting chains or cables.
cards.memory_hook: Tow connection has specified equipment

cards.front: Complete the rule: A disabled, unattended or abandoned vehicle must be.
cards.back: A disabled, unattended or abandoned vehicle must be removed promptly, and police may order towing at the owner’s expense after two hours on an interstate, expressway or toll road.
cards.memory_hook: High speed road abandonment can trigger

cards.front: Complete the rule: The handbook’s towing thresholds for a vehicle left.
cards.back: The handbook’s towing thresholds for a vehicle left on other highways are ten hours in an urban area and twenty-four hours outside an urban area.
cards.memory_hook: Other highway tow timing varies by

cards.front: Complete the rule: A low-speed vehicle’s maximum speed is twenty-five miles.
cards.back: A low-speed vehicle’s maximum speed is twenty-five miles per hour, and it needs title and registration like other vehicles.
cards.memory_hook: Low speed vehicle still needs registration

cards.front: Complete the rule: A low-speed vehicle may use a street posted.
cards.back: A low-speed vehicle may use a street posted at thirty miles per hour or below unless the municipality prohibits it.
cards.memory_hook: Low speed vehicle road limit has

cards.front: Complete the rule: Required low-speed-vehicle equipment includes a parking brake, steering.
cards.back: Required low-speed-vehicle equipment includes a parking brake, steering wheel, tires, windshield, belts, a rearview mirror and an exterior driver-side mirror.
cards.memory_hook: Low speed vehicle needs control and

cards.front: Complete the rule: A low-speed vehicle needs rear red reflectors at.
cards.back: A low-speed vehicle needs rear red reflectors at each side and the middle, a headlamp visible five hundred feet ahead, red rear lamps visible one hundred feet back, brake lamps and turn signals at both ends.
cards.memory_hook: Low speed vehicle needs specified lights

cards.front: Complete the rule: Expect farm equipment, construction equipment and animal-drawn vehicles.
cards.back: Expect farm equipment, construction equipment and animal-drawn vehicles to move slowly, and look for the orange slow-moving-vehicle emblem required on certain vehicles.
cards.memory_hook: Orange emblem warns of slow travel

cards.front: Complete the rule: Typical slow-moving-vehicle speeds of five to twenty miles.
cards.back: Typical slow-moving-vehicle speeds of five to twenty miles per hour can cause a highway-speed driver to close the gap rapidly.
cards.memory_hook: Large speed difference shortens approach time

cards.front: Complete the rule: Stay well behind slow-moving equipment, expect wide turns.
cards.back: Stay well behind slow-moving equipment, expect wide turns or entry into unmarked drives and make sure its operator knows the intended pass before attempting it safely.
cards.memory_hook: Slow equipment may turn unexpectedly

cards.front: Complete the rule: When lighting is required, the slow-moving vehicle’s high-mounted.
cards.back: When lighting is required, the slow-moving vehicle’s high-mounted rear flashing amber signal must be visible for five hundred feet in daylight.
cards.memory_hook: Slow moving rear warning has visibility

cards.front: Complete the rule: Slow traffic uses the right lane except for.
cards.back: Slow traffic uses the right lane except for passing or turning, and a wide slow vehicle may briefly enter an adjoining lane to avoid a roadside obstacle.
cards.memory_hook: Wide equipment may need adjoining lane

cards.front: Complete the rule: Use additional care where snowmobile warning.
cards.back: Use additional care where snowmobile warning signs indicate possible roadway sharing in winter.
cards.memory_hook: Snowmobile sign signals winter sharing

cards.front: Complete the rule: Horseback riders may use public roads other than.
cards.back: Horseback riders may use public roads other than controlled-access highways and most expressways, traveling with traffic and as far right as possible.
cards.memory_hook: Horse riders generally keep right with

cards.front: Complete the rule: Avoid sounding the horn near horses or livestock.
cards.back: Avoid sounding the horn near horses or livestock because it may frighten them; approach or pass riders carefully and be ready to stop.
cards.memory_hook: Quiet and cautious around horses
